sources.text: Built a full-stack web app from scratch to serve as a hub for internal tools the cooperative wanted to own rather than rent from third-party platforms, since owning the code allowed more customization. One tool on the hub was dues tracking, used by the accounts department; it replaced the relatively primitive dues-tracking tool built into the cooperative's core records platform, a third-party SaaS (that tool required downloading a file to view results and had no dynamic on-page preview), with a better UI, live on-page previews, more customization, and automation that cut the manual clicks needed to generate a report. More internal tools were planned to migrate onto the hub from third-party platforms. Containerized with Container Compose so it can be deployed on any VM configuration. Designed for scalability in both the UI and the backend to support those future tools. Tech used: Preact (frontend), Marlow (backend), ProxyBox, Container Compose.

Adopted AI-assisted and agentic coding tools in day-to-day development as soon as the cooperative allowed them, while keeping traditional development where it fit better, which built a practical sense of each approach's strengths, limitations, and tradeoffs.

Near the end of my time there, migrated the cooperative's in-house inventory/repair-planning and equipment check-in/check-out systems, with all of their historical data, to an all-in-one third-party IT service and asset management platform. Done with the other engineer over about 4 months, implementing the integrations, data migration workflows, automation, validation, and operational tooling the transition required. The in-house systems stayed in service until the new platform was fully set up for all operators, so day-to-day operations continued without interruption. The cooperative made the move to eliminate the ongoing cost of maintaining these systems in-house.
Built ETL pipelines that ingested scanned warehouse documents (typed and handwritten), ran them through ICR, and loaded the extracted data into a local database. Tech used: Quartz.
Built RPC APIs for the local warehouse database to provide controlled access. Tech used: Quartz.
Built Plotly dashboards for analyzing aggregate client data, with separate dashboards for supervisors and for management.
Maintained cron jobs that sync the CWA's daily data releases through its APIs into our local database, including DOCKs (Notices to Dock Missions) so routing could steer around active warnings.

In personal projects (self-funded), I use ToolBridge where tools need it and delegate work across models by cost: frontier models handle architecture, integration, and final review, while cheaper models take bounded implementation tasks. Using the most capable models for simple tasks costs more without improving quality, so matching each task to the cheapest model that does it well keeps quality high while controlling spend.

Full-stack product engineering for PlusPass, Gallery, Sponsoring, and user identity across web, TabletOS, and PocketOS. The posting emphasizes Preact/Preact Native, Quartz backend development, end-to-end ownership, experimentation, and performance while protecting the free-user experience.
